issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff reads no files, uses no network, pastes no coordinates and uses no labels. The new code is a crossover search (left half of one parent, right half of another, plus noise, then relaxation) over random starting layouts. The existing _relax/_score code and the final radii and validity handling are unchanged.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The crossover keeps exactly 26 circles: extras are dropped at random and missing ones are filled with random points. Centres are clipped to [0,1]. A child that fails scoring is skipped, and the loop still stops on the clock. If fewer than 2 seeds are found, the loop does not run and the code falls back to the old path.

The z value is not a real noise estimate. There is only one run per arm, so variance can't be measured. The reported z of about 11755 matches a difference of 0.0166 divided by the assumed noise floor of sqrt(2)·1e-6. Recomputed from the rounded values (-2.6131 vs -2.5965), z is about 11738. The gain of 0.0166 is real in size, but seed-to-seed variance in this stochastic search is probably far above 1e-6. One or two replicate runs are recommended before treating the gain as reliable.
Both search loops stop on the wall clock (60 s and 130 s), so how many crossover steps run depends on machine load, and results are not repeatable even with a fixed seed.

Timing margin: the search phase now runs up to 130 s instead of 80 s, adding 50 s before the unchanged refinement of the top 5. This run finished, but check the total wall time stays well inside the ~4 minute target. A slower machine could hit the 5 minute limit and crash.
The claim matches the numbers: 2.6131 is above the incumbent's 2.5965 and below the best known 2.635, which is plausible.
